title: Harvey’s Legal AI Is Now Inside Microsoft 365
format_note: Narrated walkthrough of three Microsoft integrations (SharePoint, Outlook, Word) on screen recordings, bracketed by serif title cards and a Harvey / Microsoft lockup.
one_thing: Harvey works inside the Microsoft tools lawyers already use: no switching apps, no copying files, no lost context.

transcript.voice_style: Single calm corporate narrator; continuous speech with short pauses (silence spans of 0.2-1.5 s) at section changes.
transcript.script_shape: Promise (0-20 s), one section per app (SharePoint 20 s, Outlook 34 s, Word 58 s), playbook feature, then a three-beat 'No switching apps / copying files / lost context' close and restated promise.

structure.frame0: Near-white ground with the word 'Harvey' in black serif at centre; 3 % of cells contentful (frames.frame0). Brand is present, product is not.
structure.first_3s: Harvey wordmark holds alone on white from t=0 to about 3.4 s, then 'Microsoft' fades in beside it (strips/window-01-3.417s.jpg). No product UI until t=21.7 s.

beats.what: Harvey / Microsoft lockup fades in; VO states the embedding promise.
Sharepoint, Outlook, Word icons and names stack at centre.
Three title cards: Quality at Speed, Work Without Interruption, Access Institutional Knowledge.
SharePoint: Pick files dialog, 300 files selected, Create project NDAs, upload progress.
Outlook: email thread, Summarize email, Send to Vault project, Save Email dialog, Files saved toast.
Word: prompt library, Terms That Differ Materially query, steps list, tracked redlines applied.
Word one-click workflows: fill NVCA term sheet (30 suggestions), Redact sensitive information.
Playbook run: 17 of 17 rules reviewed, redlines applied, standard positions accepted.
Six single-phrase cards: No Switching Apps ... In Sync.
Harvey / Microsoft lockup, then Harvey wordmark alone.

hero_moment.what: Playbook Summary panel shows 'Review complete 17 of 17 rules' with green, yellow, red bar as redlines land in the document margin.

ending.what: Harvey / Microsoft lockup from about 140 s, then Harvey wordmark alone to the end; no URL or call to action.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Long continuous screen-recording takes (longest shot 34.8 s, 23 % of runtime) with fast blur-to-sharp zooms inside them; hard cuts cluster at 21.7-27.7 s and 109-116 s. No burst of cuts; first cut at 21.7 s.

look.ground: Near-white (luma 232, saturation 0.012) for title cards; UI sits on a warm grey ground with soft drop shadow and a small black H mark bottom right.
look.accent_use: No brand accent; colour comes only from third-party logos and product UI (blue Outlook bar, green-yellow-red rule bar, redline red).
look.type: Title cards use a high-contrast serif (Title Case, centred, one to two lines); product UI is a clean grotesque. Cards carry no body copy.
look.depth: Flat title cards; UI windows float on a grey ground with a soft shadow (f0013.jpg) and are cropped by zoom so the window edge often leaves frame.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Screen recordings are zoomed 1.5-3x onto the active panel; whole-window wide shots at 21.7, 33-40, 100 and 120-126 s alternate with tight pushes on dialogs, toasts and the side pane.
product_ui.notes: Zoomed shots (f0016, f0028, f0029) read well, e.g. toast 'Files saved'. Wide shots (f0040, f0061, f0064) show body text under 7 px glyph height. Real recorded Outlook, Word and Vault UI with a visible cursor and hand pointer.

motion.text_entry: Cards fade in and out in place over about 0.3 s (strips/window-06-21.167s.jpg); the Microsoft logo fades in beside Harvey at 3.7-3.8 s; Sharepoint icon grows from a dot at 10.35 s then its label fades in.
motion.ui_motion: Real product animation: loading skeleton rows resolve to file list (f0012 to f0013), progress toast expands into a panel, streaming AI steps, redlines appear in the margin, suggestions apply one by one.
motion.camera: Digital zoom and pan across recordings, often with a motion-blur settle between views (f0031, strips/window-32-56.034s.jpg); the Word window drops back to a framed wide shot at 91.9 s.
motion.eases: Not measured. Zooms start with strong blur and settle sharp within about 0.3 s; no overshoot seen in strips.

transitions.cause: Title card fades to white and the Vault dialog fades up from white.
Voice moves to the next UI step; cut lands on a new dialog.
Microsoft lockup collapses to a dot that grows into the Sharepoint icon.
Zoom with motion blur travels from the Save dialog to the toast.
Upload toast expands into a panel on cursor click.

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Holds are sampled at 2 s, so about 2 s per card; 2-4 word cards need 1.1-1.7 s under the rule, so they pass. The final Harvey holds about 5 s, over the 2 s minimum.

sound.music: No music evidenced: describe tag music scores 0.078, no beat found (beats.count 0), no [music] tag in captions.
sound.sfx: None evidenced; click scores 0.082 and tick 0.059. An 'insect' tag at 0.203 is likely a speech artefact, not a design choice.
sound.vo_music_balance: Voice only: speech tag 0.915; integrated -14.7 LUFS, loudness range 4.4 LU, true peak +0.2 dBTP.
sound.energy_arc: Flat narration at about 136 words a minute with section labels A-J; short-term max -11.3 LUFS; no build or drop.
sound.sync_to_picture: Cuts are not locked to the sound: cuts_on_strong_onset_share 0.10 against chance 0.098. Closing cards do follow the phrases in the VO (about 2:06-2:14).

good.observation: The film shows real recorded UI for 70 % of runtime, zoomed onto the one panel being narrated, so each claim is visible: 'Files saved' toast, 'Review complete 17 of 17 rules'.
A short phrase card is held for each voiced idea in the close, so the take-away is readable on its own: No Switching Apps, No Copying Files, No Lost Context.
Title type is a consistent serif at 6.1-7.8 % of frame height, centred, one or two lines, three words a line at most.
Each app gets its own chapter and a before-and-after flow (select files, create project, upload; summarize, save to Vault; prompt, edit, apply), so the viewer follows cause and effect.
Microsoft lockup and app icons earn their place by naming the three integrations before any UI, then the UI follows in the same order.
Motion blur on zooms hides the jump between views and keeps the cursor path continuous through a 34.8 s take.

weak.observation: The first 21.7 s show no product, only logos and three title cards, so the film opens on brand rather than on the thing being sold.
Wide whole-window shots set body text under 7 px glyph height, unreadable at phone width, and some last 4-8 s.
Audio is a flat voiceover with no music or detectable sfx, true peak +0.2 dBTP above the -1 limit, and cuts unrelated to sound.
No call to action or URL at the end; the final 22 s are static cards (longest static run 22 s).

rule_candidates.rule: Name each integration with its logo on one card before showing any of its UI, then show the UI in the same order the card listed them.
rule_candidates.evidence: Sharepoint, Outlook, Word card at t=10.3-13 s; chapters follow at 21.7, 33, 59 s.

rule_candidates.rule: Zoom a screen recording to 1.5-3x on the panel being narrated; return to a wide window only as a 2-4 s orientation shot.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0016, f0028 zoomed; f0040, f0061 wide.

rule_candidates.rule: A wordmark-only frame 0 is acceptable for a partnership film only if the product appears within 3 s; this film waits 21.7 s and loses the hook.
Close with one phrase per card, 2-3 words each, held about 2 s, that restates the benefits in the voiceover's own words.
rule_candidates.evidence: t=128-138 s: six cards, each 2 s.

rule_candidates.rule: Set title cards at 6-8 % of frame height; this film's serif titles measure 6.1-7.8 %.
A long narrated demo can run on 4-5 s median shots and only 4 cuts a minute if zooms and UI state changes supply movement; no burst is needed.
Use blur-to-sharp zoom travel between two views of the same recording rather than a dissolve; reserve the white fade for the title-to-UI switch.
Master voice-only films at -14 LUFS but cap true peak at -1 dBTP; this film reads +0.2 dBTP.
